title: Feel like a kid again when toy car game Obstacle Overdrive launches October 2
summary: Be careful or your car will tumble to the floor and wake your parents up.
body: If you were fortunate enough to have toy cars when you were a kid—or rad enough to buy them for yourself as an adult—you probably had fun driving them over absolutely everything in your room. Mine could climb walls, scramble over book mountains, and drift around VHS-case race tracks. We'll soon be able to relive those memories without tipping pencils all over the table when Obstacle Overdrive launches October 2, 2026. Developed and published by Arcane Ermine, Obstacle Overdrive lets you go off-road—because it's all in a '90s bedroom—and make miniature radio-controlled cars navigate wacky obstacle courses. In the trailer, we see trucks going over toy keyboards, shimmying around block boards, and trundling over mountains of soft plushy toys. Wishlist Obstacle Overdrive on Steam Release date: October 2, 2026 Relive childhood memories and navigate your radio controlled cars over obstacle courses built out of toys in Obstacle Overdrive. The game launches October 2 and you can wishlist it and download the demo on Steam . Wishlist now It's important to note this isn't a racing game. There are no other people to compete with, it's just you and the track, so take your time and learn how to…

title: Virtue and a Sledgehammer announces October 27 release date with another banger of a trailer
summary: Do androids dream of electric construction tools?
body: "A machine will never hate itself enough to become better." That's the unbelievably metal quote we just saw in the latest Virtue and a Sledgehammer trailer, revealed on the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct alongside the game's launch date: October 27. We showed off some of the hammer-wielding action in our June show , so we already knew this was going to be a bizarre descent into the human psyche, as well as a game about smashing robots to bits. I love destructible environments, and I'm getting serious Red Faction: Guerrilla vibes from the carnage on offer here. What's more, these new words tell us a lot about developer Selkie Harbour's and Deconstructeam's views on self-improvement: it is fuelled by hatred, not love. title: Cairn's delayed On the Trail: Deep Water DLC gets a new release date, and you don't have long to wait
summary: The climbing game is also 20% off on Steam.
body: It felt like the moment I turned 30, all my friends got really into climbing. Pretty perfect timing then that Cairn came out when it did. We scored it 91% in our review , which is high praise indeed. For all of you impatient climbers who have been awaiting the delayed DLC, I bring good news: its new release date is only one month away. As revealed at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, the first of Cairn's free On the Trail DLC, Deep Water, will be launching October 29, 2026. This is the first of a series of free planned expansions that'll add more to the climbing game. title: Beautiful Freaks of the Desert is a speedrunning FPS flipping the middle finger at all things data center
summary: A vibey trailer announced the game for the first time at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct
body: I'm a simple man. I like first-person shooters and making jokes about AI before a combination of data center-enabled climate change and Skynet leads to the end of humanity. Beautiful Freaks of the Desert then, is poised to make me a very happy man indeed. Beautiful Freaks of the Desert's debut trailer, shown for the first time at the PC Gaming Show, does a great job of showing what the speedrunning FPS is about, using all 50 seconds to showcase intense blasting, striking title cards, and an anti-Data Center sentiment that warms my heart. Give it a watch, the trailer really does have to be seen to be believed. title: Lemonade Apocalypse has 3 simple tasks for you: Become a lemonade billionaire, 'fuel climate change,' and 'manipulate voters'
summary: Can you do that?
body: I'll tell you this right now: I'm already into what Lemonade Apocalypse is putting down. Let me count the reasons. First, its PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct reveal trailer is a very fun satire of both billionaires and the billionaire-mindset podcast industrial complex. Two, I think it will tickle the parts of my brain that just loves turning numbers into bigger numbers. Three, a lemonade apocalypse sounds much preferable to the various other apocalypses that feel like they're on table for us right now. Lemonade Apocalypse is actually a sequel to, uh, a game also called Lemonade Apocalypse. Stay with me. It's an economic simulator and incremental game where the task is to sell your soul for the dollar as quickly and dramatically as you can. "Build recipes from 70+ ingredients with evolving properties," the game's Steam page implores you, right before it also implores you to "Fuel climate change" and "Manipulate voters." title: Hello Sunshine's latest trailer has me even more excited for the giant robot game
summary: "I'm always thirsty, my feet hurt." Same.
body: A lot of games are basically escort missions dressed up in a fancy way. But in Hello Sunshine, that dynamic is flipped on its head, and you become the little sidekick that needs protecting. We just unveiled a new trailer during the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct that expands on the relationship between the Nomad and the giant robot who provides them with shelter. In the survival game, you take on the role of the Nomad, the final employee of the Sunshine Corporation that left the world a scorched ruin. In this new trailer, we hear them admit responsibility for what has happened, which is how you know you're playing a videogame, because in real life, no corpo ever admits fault. title: 'AI could never make Tenebris Somnia,' the 2D retro survival horror with live-action cutscenes and practical effects
summary: A game so emotionally scarring, "you'll call your ex."
body: I don't know if you've ever watched an Argentinian horror movie. I have, and they're damn scary. I had to watch the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct 2026 minidoc with one hand over my eyes, because Tenebris Somnia blends 2D survival horror gameplay (which I can handle) with live-action cutscenes made by an award-winning Argentinian film crew (and the make up and effects are so good they terrify me). Tenebris Somnia expertly blends a retro 2D style with filmed cutscenes. One moment you're walking through a creepy, colourful hallway, the next you're watching an actual person's face distort in a way that defies all logic and reason. Dave Oshry, CEO of New Blood Interactive, the publisher of the game, hypes up the practical effects crew, but I'm pretty certain they just cast real demons. title: Vaewolf's new story trailer takes us down a brutal path of revenge, and shows off the frenetic vampire and werewolf combat
summary: Part vampire, part werewolf, part elf, all fury.
body: It's always vampires versus werewolves. In games like Skyrim, you can be one or the other, but not both. In Twilight, you had to choose team Jacob or team Edward. Now we're all grown up, it's team Charlie and Carlisle all the way. In Vaewolf, you don't have to choose, you play an elf who's half werewolf and half vampire. Vaewolf is an action game where you hack and slash your way to vengeance. The PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct just debuted a story trailer that gives us a good look at the events that led to our protagonist going down the path of violence. Wishlist Vaewolf on Steam Release date: Early 2027 Part werewolf, part vampire, and part elf? Well that's certainly a mix we didn't see coming. Vaewolf is a frenetic action game coming early 2027. Wishlist it on Steam . Wishlist now Werewolves destroyed their village, leaving them as the only survivor. They must have been nicked by a claw or tooth, because they can transform into a devastatingly powerful werewolf form and smash through enemies. I'm not too sure where the vampire form comes into things, though. Maybe they got bitten later? Or maybe they were always a vampire and that's how they survived the doggo attack? I don't know…

title: Stronghold 4 boasts castles aplenty and a rogue's gallery of weirdos to pit them against
summary: Sign me up, m'lord.
body: Since the dawn of time, mankind has reckoned with one overriding question: how do I get in that building and kill everyone in it? For almost as long, the Stronghold series has grappled with both sides of this conundrum, placing you in the mailed shoes of both defender and attacker in medieval siege after medieval siege. Now, 15 years (would you believe it?) after Stronghold 3, Stronghold 4 is here to put things in trebuchets and launch them at you, and we just caught sight of it at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct. title: A 27-year-old tech forum with over 100,000 Warcraft 3 modding threads is closing its doors
summary: "The site will be archived. The content will be available for people if they want it."
body: "Anyone want help on anything." That's the title of the oldest post I could dig up on The Helper's Warcraft 3 world editor help forum, posted by Neo_HoJo all the way back in July 2002. It's one of over 100,000 similar threads, collectively containing approximately 859,700 comments. It seems to be the biggest forum on the site by far. But just as Warcraft 3 grapples once again for a new lease on life , The Helper is turning in. The announcement came in the form of a post from an admin also called The Helper. "Wow, it's been a ride," the post reads. "Over 27 years of this site from a personal homepage, to a Blizzard [games] tech support site, a world editor help site, and then a community of helpers from then until now. "[For many years] I was a lost soul floating around the dark side of the Internet, skimming the edges and really just not having any kind of focus. That has changed. I am no longer a lost soul. I am now on Team Jesus and unfortunately my path moving forward does not include having this site competing for my time … The site will be archived. The content will be available for people if they want it. It just will not be advertised or out there in any forum that bots or …
